items.title: Submit proof of use of Bauspardarlehen funds
items.quote: Bitte reichen Sie den Nachweis binnen 10 Arbeitstagen nach dem Briefdatum ein.
items.computation: Letter date (Briefdatum) is Sat 21.11.2026. This is a company letter, so no statutory deemed-delivery rule applies; the letter itself fixes the start as the 'Briefdatum'. Under § 187 Abs. 1 BGB the day of the event (21.11.) is not counted, so counting starts 22.11.2026. Counting 10 Arbeitstage (Mon-Fri, excluding public holidays, per the letter's own definition and § 193 BGB): skip Sun 22.11, Sat 28.11 and Sun 29.11 as non-business days; no public holiday falls in the window. The 10th business day after 21.11.2026 is Fri 04.12.2026. That day is itself a business day, so no further shift is needed.

items.title: Loan payout delayed to start of next month if proof is late
items.quote: Geht der Nachweis nicht rechtzeitig ein, verschiebt sich die Auszahlung auf den nächsten Monatsersten.
items.computation: This is a consequence, not a separate deadline for the recipient to act on: if the proof deadline of 04.12.2026 is missed, payout moves to the first of the following calendar month. Given relative to the 04.12.2026 deadline, the next month's first day would be 01.01.2027, but the exact date depends on how late the proof actually arrives, so this is only the earliest/illustrative consequence date, not a fixed due date.

warnings: This is a private company (Bausparkasse) letter, not an authority letter, so the statutory 'deemed delivery' rules for administrative post do not apply; the deadline was computed from the printed 'Briefdatum' itself, as the letter instructs ('binnen 10 Arbeitstagen nach dem Briefdatum'), so please confirm the envelope's actual postmark/receipt date if it differs from 21.11.2026.

The consequence clause ('Auszahlung verschiebt sich auf den nächsten Monatsersten') is vague about which month-first applies if the proof arrives a few days late versus very late; treat the 2027-01-01 date given as illustrative only, not a guaranteed date.

The IBAN printed (DE69 3705 0198 0005 5525 20) is well-formed and matches a German bank code, but this letter does not ask for a payment to this account — it is only the sender's general contact IBAN; no action needed unless asked to pay.
